The Government Agent or any person duly authorized by him in writing may at any time of the day between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. enter any land alienated on a permit or holding for the purpose of inspection or for any other purpose incidental to or connected with the duties of a Government Agent under this Ordinance.

body.heading: No prescriptive title to be acquired to land alienated under Ordinance.
body.raw_text: 161. No person shall, by possession of any land alienated on a permit, acquire any prescriptive title thereto against any other person or against the State.

body.heading: Notary attesting deed in breach of section 162 guilty of offence
body.raw_text: 163.A notary who knowingly attests any deed in breach of the provisions of section 162 shall be guilty of an offence and shall, on conviction by a Magistrate after summary trial, be liable to a fine not exceeding five hundred rupees.

body.heading: Mapped-out land may be settled
body.raw_text: 164.The fact that any land has been mapped-out shall be no bar to the inclusion of such land in a settlement notice under the Land Settlement Ordinance.

body.heading: Action re vindicatio may be maintained against State in respect of alienated land.
body.raw_text: 165.(1) Nothing in this Ordinance contained shall preclude any person claiming to be entitled to any land which has been alienated from instituting an action against the State for the vindication of his title thereto; but nothing in this section shall enable or authorize the owner of a holding or a permit-holder to sue the State for the vindication of title to such holding or to the land alienated to such permit-holder, as the case may be.

body.heading: Loans to permit- holders who are paying annual sums by virtue of provisions of section 19A (3)T
body.raw_text: 172. Regulations may be made for lending money to permit-holders who are paying an annual instalment by virtue of the provisions of section 19* out of funds provided for the purpose by Parliament. Such regulations may prescribe the conditions upon which and the terms for which such money may be lent. Where default is made in the repayment of any money lent to such a permit-holder under this section such money together with the interest, if any, which is due thereon shall be deemed to be money due to the State under this Ordinance and may be recovered in the manner hereinbefore provided in Chapter X.
